items.title: MCP server permanently gives up after a transient backend outage; never reconnects until gateway restart
items.body:
## Summary

A streamable-HTTP MCP server that drops during a **transient** backend outage is permanently marked dead and is never reconnected, even after the backend becomes healthy again. The only recovery is a full gateway restart. By contrast, LLM API calls (`agent.conversation_loop`) retry per-call and self-heal, so the agent's "brain" recovers while its MCP tools stay broken indefinitely.

## Environment

- hermes-agent `0.14.0` (Docker image `nousresearch/hermes-agent:sha-ba9964f…`), self-hosted, single gateway.
- Two MCP servers configured over **streamable-HTTP** (`mcp_servers.<name>.url`), each on a different backend host.
- Backends reachable over normal LAN; no auth header on the MCP transport.

## What happened

Both backend hosts were powered down briefly (planned, ~1 min — a storm). At that instant **both** MCP servers lost their connections simultaneously. Each ran its reconnect budget (5 attempts, ~31s of exponential backoff) while the backends were still down, then gave up:

```
00:47:59 WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'mealie'  connection lost (attempt 1/5), reconnecting in 1s: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
00:48:03 WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'mealie'  connection lost (attempt 2/5), reconnecting in 2s: ...
00:48:06 WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'mealie'  connection lost (attempt 3/5), reconnecting in 4s: ...
00:48:13 WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'mealie'  connection lost (attempt 4/5), reconnecting in 8s: ...
00:48:43 WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'mealie'  failed after 5 reconnection attempts, giving up: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
# identical sequence for the second server ('crawl4ai') on a different host
```

The backends came back ~1 minute later. **15 hours on**, every tool call still returns:

```
WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool mcp_<name>_<tool> returned error: {"error": "MCP server '<name>' is not connected"}
```

The MCP endpoints were verified healthy and reachable from inside the gateway container throughout (a manual HTTPS request to the `/mcp` URL returns a normal response). Only Hermes' view of the connection is stale. A gateway restart fully restores both servers.

## Root cause

In `tools/mcp_tool.py`, the server lifecycle loop (`MCPServerTask.run`) treats reconnection as a **bounded, one-shot budget**. After `_MAX_RECONNECT_RETRIES` (`= 5`) failures:

```python
# tools/mcp_tool.py ~L1638
retries += 1
if retries > _MAX_RECONNECT_RETRIES:
    logger.warning(
        "MCP server '%s' failed after %d reconnection attempts, giving up: %s",
        self.name, _MAX_RECONNECT_RETRIES, exc,
    )
    return   # <-- the server Task exits permanently
```

Once `run()` returns, the Task is gone. Nothing re-probes the server, and `_reconnect_event` has no listener anymore, so even an external trigger (e.g. `/mcp` refresh setting `_reconnect_event`) can't revive a Task that already returned. The reconnect budget (~31s) is far shorter than a routine backend reboot, so any outage longer than ~30s is effectively permanent.

This is asymmetric with the LLM transport: `agent.conversation_loop` retries each API call independently, so a backend that returns later is picked up automatically.

## Suggested fix (any of)

1. **Never permanently give up on a configured server.** After exhausting the fast reconnect budget, drop into a slow background re-probe loop (capped backoff, e.g. 30–60s) instead of `return`. The server reconnects on its own once the backend is healthy — matching the LLM-call resilience model.
2. **Make a dead server revivable.** Keep a supervisor that can restart a `run()` that has exited, so `/mcp` refresh (or a keepalive) can bring it back without a full gateway restart.
3. At minimum, **surface the permanently-dead state** distinctly (not just a one-line WARNING at give-up) so operators can alert on it — the only current signal is per-tool-call "is not connected" errors after the fact.

(1) matches user expectation best: a configured MCP server should converge back to connected on its own once reachable, the same way the model endpoint does.

## Possibly related

#31346 (SSE MCP `CancelledError` on Cloud Run) — different trigger/exception, but same family (MCP transport teardown not recovering).

items.title: Desktop: persist draft prompt text when navigating away from a new session
items.body:
## Bug Description

In the desktop app, draft prompt text in a newly created session is lost if the user navigates away before submitting it and then returns to that new session.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a new session in the desktop app.
2. Start typing a prompt in the chat input.
3. Before submitting, click into another session or another page/settings area of the app.
4. Return to the new session.

## Actual Behavior

The partially written prompt is gone, so the user has to start over.

## Expected Behavior

The draft prompt should persist per session until one of these happens:

- The user submits the prompt.
- The user explicitly clears/deletes the draft.
- The session itself is deleted/reset in a way that should discard drafts.

## Motivation

This is a common workflow: start composing a new prompt, realize you need to reference something from another session or check a setting/context, navigate away briefly, then come back and finish. Losing the draft is a paper-cut that makes the desktop app feel brittle.

## Proposed Solution

Persist unsent input text keyed by session ID, at least in local UI state and ideally through app reloads if that fits the architecture. New-session drafts should behave like lightweight per-session memory rather than being tied only to the mounted chat input component.

## Environment

- App: Hermes Agent desktop application
- Area: New session / chat composer draft state

items.title: /title slash command doesn't rename session on Windows Desktop
items.body:
## Bug Description

The `/title` slash command does not persist the session name change on Hermes Desktop for Windows. The command is accepted (no error), but the session title remains unchanged.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop on Windows 11
2. Start a conversation
3. Type `/title New Session Name` and press Enter
4. Observe that the session title does NOT change

## Expected Behavior

The session should be renamed immediately after issuing `/title`.

## Actual Behavior

The command is accepted silently, but the title stays the same.

## Workaround

The CLI works correctly:

```
hermes sessions list
hermes sessions rename <SESSION_ID> "New Title"
```

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Hermes Desktop (installed at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`)
- Provider: OpenRouter
- TTS: edge, STT: local

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

In SSH connection mode on Windows, sending a voice message fails with:

```
Error invoking remote method 'transcribe-audio': Error: Transcription failed (400). 
{"error":{"message":"invalid content-type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----formdata-undici-038107429163","code":400}}
```

The transcription is attempted locally (Electron main process uses undici HTTP client) rather than forwarded to the remote Hermes via the SSH tunnel.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Hermes Desktop on Windows 11, SSH mode to remote VPS
2. Record and send a voice message
3. Error appears immediately

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Hermes Desktop (SSH mode → Ubuntu 24.04 VPS)
- Remote server has faster-whisper installed and Telegram voice transcription works fine
- No faster-whisper installed locally on Windows
- Desktop installed at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`
- Config: connectionMode=ssh, provider=openrouter

## Workaround

Voice transcription works correctly via Telegram gateway on the same remote server.

items.title: hermes update repeatedly autostashes Desktop bootstrap marker .hermes-bootstrap-complete

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
# hermes update repeatedly autostashes Desktop bootstrap marker `.hermes-bootstrap-complete`

## Bug description

After Hermes Desktop/bootstrap creates `$HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent/.hermes-bootstrap-complete`, `hermes update` treats that marker as an untracked local change because it lives inside the managed git checkout and is not ignored by `.gitignore`.

The updater then runs `git stash push --include-untracked`, prompts the user to restore local changes, and creates an autostash even though the only "local change" was generated by Hermes itself.

This can repeat across updates:

- If the user restores the stash, the marker comes back as an untracked file, making the checkout dirty again for the next update.
- If the user skips restoration, the Desktop bootstrap marker remains only in the stash, which can make later Desktop launches take the bootstrap/setup path again.

This is confusing UX because the prompt frames the marker as user local customization, but it is Hermes-managed runtime/install state.

## Observed behavior

On macOS after running `hermes update`, the update created an autostash and prompted:

```text
→ Local changes detected — stashing before update...
Saved working directory and index state On main: hermes-update-autostash-20260603-224117
...
⚠ Local changes were stashed before updating.
  Restoring them may reapply local customizations onto the updated codebase.
  Review the result afterward if Hermes behaves unexpectedly.
Restore local changes now? [Y/n]
```

The user chose not to restore. Inspecting the resulting stashes showed that both recent update autostashes contained only the Desktop bootstrap marker:

```text
--- status --short ---

--- stashes include-untracked ---
===== stash@{0} =====
 .hermes-bootstrap-complete | 8 ++++++++
 1 file changed, 8 insertions(+)
===== stash@{1} =====
 .hermes-bootstrap-complete | 8 ++++++++
 1 file changed, 8 insertions(+)
--- current marker ---
missing
```

The marker content was normal Hermes bootstrap metadata:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "pinnedCommit": "ecac659d7da3b95c9f518e5038ee29fd77bb040a",
  "pinnedBranch": null,
  "adopted": true,
  "completedAt": "2026-06-03T15:47:14.862Z",
  "desktopVersion": "0.15.1"
}
```

## Expected behavior

Hermes-generated runtime/bootstrap markers should not make the managed install checkout appear user-modified, and should not trigger a restore prompt during `hermes update`.

`hermes update` should only stash user-meaningful local changes, not known Hermes-managed state files.

## Relevant code / state

The updater dirty-checks the whole checkout and then includes untracked files in the stash:

```python
# hermes_cli/main.py::_stash_local_changes_if_needed
status = subprocess.run(git_cmd + ["status", "--porcelain"], ...)
...
subprocess.run(
    git_cmd + ["stash", "push", "--include-untracked", "-m", stash_name],
    ...
)
```

The Desktop app deliberately places the marker inside the active checkout:

```js
// apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs
const ACTIVE_HERMES_ROOT = path.join(HERMES_HOME, 'hermes-agent')
const BOOTSTRAP_COMPLETE_MARKER = path.join(ACTIVE_HERMES_ROOT, '.hermes-bootstrap-complete')
```

Current `.gitignore` ignores many local/runtime/build outputs, but not `.hermes-bootstrap-complete`.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5.1, arm64
- Hermes Agent: 0.15.1
- Python: 3.11.3
- Node: v22.17.0
- npm: 11.10.1
- Install path: `/Users/Andrea/.hermes/hermes-agent`
- Current commit after update: `51a2c0701 fix(skills): document xurl X Article ingestion`
- Desktop packaged app exists at: `/Users/Andrea/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/mac-arm64/Hermes.app`

## Possible fixes

1. Add `.hermes-bootstrap-complete` to the repository `.gitignore`.
2. Teach `hermes update` to ignore known Hermes-generated runtime markers when deciding whether a stash is needed.
3. Move the bootstrap marker outside the git checkout and migrate existing installs.

The smallest fix is likely option 1, but option 2 may still be useful so the updater's dirty check distinguishes user changes from Hermes-managed runtime state.

## Related issues / PRs

- #3523: `hermes update` unnecessary stashes / silent fetch regressions
- #20112: pending PR to reduce unnecessary stashes when already up to date
- #6357: update UX should show where to run `git status`
- #37554 / #37674: Desktop bootstrap/onboarding marker behavior

This issue is distinct from #3523 because it can still occur when there are real updates to pull: the checkout is considered dirty solely because Hermes created `.hermes-bootstrap-complete` as an untracked marker inside the repo.

items.title: [Bug]: Pinned HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN in .env breaks Desktop LOCAL mode into SIGTERM boot loop

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description A `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` left pinned in `~/.hermes/.env` puts the Desktop app into an unrecoverable boot loop **in local mode**. The app repeatedly logs `Hermes backend is ready` -> `Restarting desktop connection` -> `Hermes backend exited (SIGTERM)` and the renderer shows a "Could not connect to Hermes Gateway" error, even though the spawned local backend is healthy and listening. This is the inverse of the existing remote-gateway issues (#38332, #38115, #38266): here the **remote feature's required setting poisons local mode** after the user reverts to local. The token is a remote-backend requirement per the docs at `/docs/user-guide/desktop#connecting-to-a-remote-backend`, but nothing clears or ignores it when `connection.json` is back to `{"mode":"local","remote":{"url":""}}`. ## Root Cause (confirmed by fix) In local mode the Desktop spawns its own `hermes_cli.main dashboard --tui --host 127.0.0.1 --port

` backend and manages the dashboard session token handshake automatically. When `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` is pinned in `.env`, the local backend enforces that fixed token while the local renderer presents the auto-generated one. They never match, the desktop's readiness/auth check fails, it SIGTERMs the backend it just spawned, and restarts -- forever. Notably the backend process itself is fine: `lsof` shows it LISTENing, it answers HTTP, and the process is correctly parented to the Electron app (not an orphan). The failure is purely the token mismatch in the readiness handshake. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Follow the remote-backend docs and set `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN=` in `~/.hermes/.env` (as instructed to pin a stable token). 2. Later turn **Settings -> Gateway -> Remote gateway** back OFF (or never finish remote setup), so `connection.json` is `{"mode":"local","remote":{"url":""}}`. 3. Launch the Desktop app. 4. Observe the boot loop in `~/.hermes/logs/desktop.log`: ``` [boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup [boot] Restarting desktop connection Hermes backend exited (SIGTERM) [boot] Resolving Hermes backend ... repeats ... ``` ## Expected Behavior In local mode the Desktop/backend should ignore a pinned `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` (or auto-rotate its own), so a leftover remote-setup artifact cannot break local startup. At minimum, surface a clear diagnostic ("pinned dashboard token present but app is in local mode -- token will be ignored / remove it") instead of an opaque SIGTERM loop and a generic "Could not connect" error. ## Actual Behavior Infinite SIGTERM/restart loop; renderer shows "Could not connect to Hermes Gateway." No log line names the token mismatch as the cause, making this very hard to diagnose -- the symptom looks identical to the orphaned-backend port-collision loop, which sends you down the wrong path. ## Workaround Comment out the pinned token and relaunch: ```bash # in ~/.hermes/.env #HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN= pkill -f "Hermes.app/Contents/MacOS/Hermes"; pkill -f "hermes_cli.main dashboard" open -a Hermes ``` Confirmed: removing the pin clears the loop and the app reaches the main chat page on the next launch. ## Environment - Desktop: 0.15.1 (bootstrap pinned commit `51a2c07016b2bf263d4a863cbe8de316f05132ab`, branch main) - OS: macOS 26.5.1 - Backend Python: 3.11.15 - Install: git (NousResearch fork), `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` - Mode: local (`connection.json` mode=local, empty remote url) ## Suggested Fix Directions - Local-mode backend resolution should not honor `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` from `.env`; treat that var as remote-only, or scope it so it only applies when `connection.json` mode is remote. - Add a startup guard in the Electron main process: if `mode==local` and a pinned dashboard token is detected, log a named warning and bypass it rather than failing the readiness check. ## Related - #38332 (remote reaches backend but UI shows startup error / falls back to local unless env-forced) - #38115 (remote SIGTERM -> WS 1012 loop; "Test remote" false-passes) - #38266 (remote reconnect loop after successful connection)

items.title: execute_code tool blocked in cron mode — data processing downgrades to fragile workarounds

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## The Problem

`execute_code` is one of Hermes' most powerful tools — it lets the agent write Python that calls other tools, processes intermediate results, and makes conditional decisions. But it is **completely unavailable in cron mode**, blocked by the interactive approval requirement.

This creates a capability cliff: the same agent that can process data and branch on conditions during interactive sessions degrades to manual workarounds when automated.

## Why This Matters

### 1. The cron fallback is fragile

Without `execute_code`, the only way to do data processing in cron is:

```python
# Write a temp script
write_file("/tmp/parser.py", content)
# Pipe curl into it
terminal("curl ... | python3 /tmp/parser.py")
# Hope the temp file doesn't collide with another cron run
# Hope the parser handles all edge cases without interactive debugging
```

This fails in production:
- Two cron jobs running simultaneously can clobber `/tmp/parser.py`
- A parser that works in interactive mode breaks silently in cron because the agent can't iterate
- The agent can't inspect intermediate results before deciding next steps — it's all-or-nothing

### 2. The capability gap is inconsistent

Consider what the agent can do in cron WITHOUT `execute_code`:
- `terminal("python3 -c '...'")` — run arbitrary Python as a one-liner
- `terminal("python3 /some/script.py")` — run an existing script
- `terminal("curl ... | python3 -c '...'")` — pipe data through Python

All of these are executing arbitrary Python. The only difference with `execute_code` is that the agent can:
- See intermediate results and branch on them
- Call other tools programmatically within the same code block
- Handle errors gracefully with try/except

The security model already permits arbitrary code execution via `terminal`. Blocking `execute_code` doesn't prevent code execution — it only prevents *reasoned, multi-step* code execution.

### 3. Real-world impact

From running Hermes in production with 20+ cron jobs:

| Task | Without execute_code | With execute_code |
|---|---|---|
| Parse arXiv API XML | Write parser to temp file, pipe curl, hope no concurrent run | Read XML, parse, branch on results, write entities |
| Filter & rank research papers | Cannot do multi-step: search → parse → compare → rank → write | One code block does it all |
| Verify data integrity after cron job | Terminal SQL query, can't branch on result | Query → check thresholds → alert if needed |
| Reconcile index counts | Manual grep/awk (see knowledge-management skill) | Direct Python: count files, diff IDs, patch |

Every one of these required a workaround. The temp-file pattern appears in multiple production skills as "⚠️ cron mode no execute_code fallback" sections.

## Root Cause

The approval requirement for `execute_code` makes sense in interactive mode — the user should approve code that has full Python + tool access. But in cron mode, the user has already approved the job itself. The job's prompt and skills define its scope. Blocking `execute_code` inside an already-approved cron job is double-gating.

## Proposed Solution

A `cron_mode` config option that, when enabled, allows `execute_code` in cron jobs:

```yaml
security:
  execute_code:
    cron_mode: auto_approve  # or 'block' (default), or 'sandbox'
```

- **`block`** (default): current behavior, safe for most users
- **`auto_approve`**: auto-approve execute_code in cron context. The principle: user approved the cron job → execute_code inherits that approval
- **`sandbox`**: future option — run in a restricted subprocess without tool access, purely for data processing

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Add `--non-interactive` flag to execute_code tool**: Changes the approval model per-invocation rather than per-session. More granular but more complex.
2. **Allow execute_code but strip tool-calling imports**: The agent gets `import pandas, json, re` but not `from hermes_tools import ...`. Safest option, covers 80% of cron use cases (data processing).
3. **Status quo**: Keep blocking it and accept the temp-file workaround pattern as "by design."

## Relationship to Existing Work

- **#31970** (hermes mcp add lacks non-interactive flag): Same pattern — tool works interactively but breaks in automation. The underlying issue is that Hermes tools were designed for interactive use and automation was bolted on later.
- **cron job approvals model**: Cron jobs already have a distinct approval model (they bypass the shell-command approval that interactive sessions require). This proposal extends that principle to code execution.

## Open Questions

1. Should `auto_approve` be per-job or global?
2. If we strip tool imports (alternative 2), does that satisfy enough use cases?
3. Should sandboxing use the same mechanism as the code execution sandbox, or something simpler?
4. Is there a middle ground where `execute_code` in cron can call `terminal`/`web_search` but not `write_file`/`patch`?

---

*Issue from production use with 20+ cron jobs. At least 5 of them would be simpler, faster, and less fragile with `execute_code` available. The temp-file workaround pattern has caused silent failures when concurrent cron runs collided.*

items.title: [Feature]: Desktop Client-Only Installation
items.body:
### Problem or Use Case
Install Hermes Desktop as thin-client connecting to remote hermes installation.

---

## The Reality

The desktop app is designed to always bootstrap the Hermes Agent runtime on first launch if no installation is found. [2](#3-1)  The bootstrap runner in `electron/main.cjs` automatically runs `install.ps1` stages to install Python, Node, and other dependencies. [3](#3-2) 

## Remote Mode Workaround

If you set these environment variables **before first launch**, the desktop app will connect to a remote backend and skip the local backend spawn:

```bash
HERMES_DESKTOP_REMOTE_URL=https://your-remote-backend.com/hermes
HERMES_DESKTOP_REMOTE_TOKEN=your-session-token
```

When these are set, `resolveRemoteBackend()` returns a remote configuration and `startHermes()` connects to it immediately, never reaching the local backend code path. [4](#3-3) [1](#3-0) 

## Limitations

- The Electron shell itself is still installed (that's the desktop app)
- If you ever unset the environment variables, the app will attempt to bootstrap the local runtime on next launch
- There's no official "client-only" build that excludes the bootstrap logic entirely

## Notes

The bootstrap logic is in `ensureRuntime()` which only runs when `backend.kind === 'bootstrap-needed'` — meaning no usable local installation was found. [3](#3-2)  Remote mode via environment variables is the intended way to use the desktop app without a local backend, but it doesn't prevent the initial bootstrap attempt if the env vars aren't set before first launch.


### Proposed Solution

Flag for installer that doesn't install or run server components.

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

Other

### Scope

Small (single file, < 50 lines)

items.title: Update reports 7 commits behind / remains on 0.15.1 when main differs from latest release tag 0.15.2

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, after running `hermes update`, Hermes remained on `v0.15.1` and continued reporting:

```text
Update available: 7 commits behind — run 'hermes update'
```

However, the official latest release appears to be `v0.15.2 (2026.5.29.2)`, available via tag `v2026.5.29.2`. The current `main` branch was up to date but still had `pyproject.toml` version `0.15.1`.

This made the updater behavior confusing: `main` appeared current, but the official release version was newer.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Shell: PowerShell
- Hermes project path: `C:\Users\Srika\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent`
- Python: 3.11.15
- Node.js: v24.15.0

## Initial state after `hermes update`

```powershell
hermes --version
```

Output:

```text
Hermes Agent v0.15.1 (2026.5.29)
Project: C:\Users\Srika\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent
Python: 3.11.15
OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0
Update available: 7 commits behind — run 'hermes update'
```

`hermes doctor` showed Python environment/version files were consistent at `0.15.1`, and the gateway was healthy.

## Git state before manual tag switch

```powershell
cd "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\hermes-agent"
git status
git log --oneline -5
git log --oneline HEAD..origin/main
```

Output:

```text
On branch main
Your branch is up to date with 'origin/main'.

nothing to commit, working tree clean

04d620d91 (HEAD -> main, origin/main, origin/HEAD) fix(docker): run config migrations during container boot (salvage #35508) (#36627)
92be98929 Merge pull request #38564 from NousResearch/bb/tui-sgr-mouse-fragment-leak
343c54e35 fix(docker): reject unsupported --user <arbitrary-uid> start with clear guidance (#38579)
b0a52d74a fix(mcp): resolve ${ENV} in discovery probe so header auth works (#38571)
5a22cd427 fix(desktop): configure local/custom endpoint without an API key or UI changes
```

`git log --oneline HEAD..origin/main` returned no commits, confirming local `main` was current.

But `main` still showed:

```powershell
Select-String -Path .\pyproject.toml -Pattern 'version'
```

Output:

```text
pyproject.toml:10:version = "0.15.1"
```

## Release tag check

```powershell
git fetch --tags origin
git tag --sort=-creatordate | Select-Object -First 20
```

Output included:

```text
v2026.5.29.2
v2026.5.29
v2026.5.28
...
```

Checking the release tag:

```powershell
git show v2026.5.29.2:pyproject.toml | Select-String -Pattern 'version'
```

Output:

```text
version = "0.15.2"
```

So the latest release tag had `0.15.2`, but current `main` had `0.15.1`.

## Workaround used

Stopped the gateway, switched to the release tag, and reinstalled editable package:

```powershell
hermes gateway stop
cd "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\hermes-agent"
git switch --detach v2026.5.29.2
.\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e .
```

After that:

```powershell
hermes --version
```

Output:

```text
Hermes Agent v0.15.2 (2026.5.29.2)
Project: C:\Users\Srika\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent
Python: 3.11.15
OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0
Update available: 7 commits behind — run 'hermes update'
```

Gateway then started successfully:

```powershell
hermes gateway start
hermes gateway status
```

Output:

```text
✓ Gateway started via Scheduled Task 'Hermes_Gateway' (PID: 10988)
✓ Scheduled Task registered: Hermes_Gateway
  Status: Ready
  Last Run Time: 04-06-2026 07:00:20
  Last Run Result: 0
✓ Gateway process running (PID: 10988)
```

## Expected behavior

If `v0.15.2` / `v2026.5.29.2` is the official latest release, `hermes update` should either:

1. Install/switch to the latest release tag, or
2. Clearly explain that it tracks `main`, not the latest release tag, or
3. Avoid reporting the user is behind if `main` is current but a release tag has a higher package version.

## Actual behavior

- `hermes update` left the install on `0.15.1`.
- `main` was current and clean.
- Official release tag `v2026.5.29.2` had `pyproject.toml` version `0.15.2`.
- After manually switching to the tag and reinstalling, `hermes --version` correctly showed `v0.15.2`, but still reported `Update available: 7 commits behind` because the detached release tag is behind `main`.

## Why this matters

This is confusing for users because the CLI says to run `hermes update`, but following `main` may keep the package at `0.15.1` while the GitHub release is `0.15.2`. It is not obvious whether users should track `main` or the latest release tag.

labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

The Dashboard (`/skills`) and Desktop app expose a skills toggle UI, but it only affects the default profile (`~/.hermes/skills/`). Each profile has its own isolated `skills/` directory (`~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/skills/`), but there is no UI to manage them — it requires CLI commands like `researcher skills config`or moving files via finder.

The `/profiles` page already lists profiles with edit capabilities, but has no skills enable or disable.

## Proposed Solution

Add a **Skills** section to each profile edit page on `/profiles`. When a user clicks into a profile (e.g. `researcher`), show the same toggle UI that exists on `/skills`, scoped to that profile's `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/skills/` directory.

- List all installed skills for that profile with enable/disable toggles
- Disable keeps the skill installed but marks it inactive (same as existing disable behavior on `/skills`)
- Enable re-activates it without re-installation
- Changes write to the profile's skills config, not the default profile's

## Context

- Dashboard profiles page already exists: `http://127.0.0.1:9119/profiles`
- Skills toggle UI already exists: `http://127.0.0.1:9119/skills`
- Related but more scoped than #10674 and #13547 (which propose a full profile switcher across the dashboard)
- This could be implemented as a first step toward broader multi-profile dashboard support

items.title: Windows: Two bugs in cron `_run_job_script` — pythonw.exe loses stdout + GBK encoding crash
items.body:
# Windows: Two bugs in cron `_run_job_script` — pythonw.exe loses stdout + GBK encoding crash

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 11 Pro (Build 22631)
- **Hermes**: v0.14.0 (also confirmed present in v0.15.2 source)
- **Python**: 3.14.3 (also affects 3.11 via uv)
- **Locale**: Chinese (Simplified), system code page GBK (936)
- **Launch method**: `hermes` gateway (uses `pythonw.exe` as `sys.executable`)

## Bug 1: `pythonw.exe` has no console — `subprocess.run(capture_output=True)` returns empty stdout

### Problem

On Windows, when Hermes is launched as `pythonw.exe` (the GUI-subsystem Python), `sys.executable` points to `pythonw.exe`. The cron scheduler uses this to run job scripts:

```python
# scheduler.py line ~928
argv = [sys.executable, str(path)]
```

When `pythonw.exe` runs a child `pythonw.exe` process, the child has **no console**. Python's `sys.stdout` in a console-less process is either `None` or fully buffered with no flush target. Even with `print(..., flush=True)`, `sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)`, or `os.write(1, ...)`, the output is lost when `subprocess.run(capture_output=True, text=True)` reads the pipe — the subprocess reader thread reads an empty buffer.

### Impact

All `no_agent=True` cron jobs with `.py` scripts produce **empty stdout** on Windows. The scheduler treats this as "nothing to report" and never delivers the output. Effectively, `no_agent=True` Python scripts are **completely broken on Windows**.

### Evidence

This error appears in the **gateway console window** (stdout of the `hermes` gateway process), not in agent.log:

```
Exception in thread Thread-3 (_readerthread):
  File "...\Lib\threading.py", line 1045, in _bootstrap_inner
  File "...\Lib\subprocess.py", line 1599, in _readerthread
    buffer.append(fh.read())
UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xad in position 14: illegal multibyte sequence
```

The gateway process (running as `pythonw.exe`) spawns the cron scheduler, which in turn runs `subprocess.run(capture_output=True, text=True)` for the job script. The GBK crash in the reader thread proves the script DID run and produce output — the encoding failure crashes the thread, yielding empty stdout.

This is particularly insidious because: the gateway console is typically hidden (pythonw.exe has no visible window), so the user sees **no error at all** — just silent cron job failures.

### Suggested Fix

```python
# In the else branch (Python interpreter):
if sys.platform == "win32" and sys.executable.lower().endswith("pythonw.exe"):
    # pythonw.exe has no console — stdout is lost in subprocess capture.
    # Use python.exe (console subsystem) from the same directory instead.
    python_exe = Path(sys.executable).parent / "python.exe"
    if python_exe.is_file():
        argv = [str(python_exe), str(path)]
    else:
        argv = [sys.executable, str(path)]
else:
    argv = [sys.executable, str(path)]
```

## Bug 2: `subprocess.run(text=True)` uses GBK on Chinese Windows — crashes on non-ASCII output

### Problem

```python
# scheduler.py line ~944
result = subprocess.run(
    argv,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,        # ← uses locale.getpreferredencoding() = 'gbk' on Chinese Windows
    timeout=script_timeout,
    ...
)
```

On Chinese Windows, `text=True` defaults to GBK (code page 936). If a cron script prints any Chinese characters (or any non-GBK byte), the subprocess reader thread throws `UnicodeDecodeError`, which causes `stdout` to be empty.

### Impact

Any cron job script that outputs non-ASCII text (Chinese, Japanese, emoji, etc.) will crash the reader thread and produce empty stdout. This is not hypothetical — my SSH login monitor script outputs Chinese alert text and hits this immediately.

### Suggested Fix

```python
result = subprocess.run(
    argv,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    encoding="utf-8",     # ← explicit encoding, not locale-dependent
    errors="replace",     # ← graceful fallback instead of crash
    timeout=script_timeout,
    cwd=str(path.parent),
    env=run_env,
    **popen_kwargs,
)
```

## Workaround (current)

I'm currently working around both bugs by:
1. Using only English output in my cron scripts (avoids GBK crash)
2. Patching `scheduler.py` locally to add `encoding="utf-8"` and swap `pythonw.exe` → `python.exe`

## Reproduction

1. Install Hermes on Chinese Windows 11
2. Create a cron job with `no_agent=True` and a Python script:
   ```python
   # test_cron.py
   print("Hello 你好")  # Chinese characters
   ```
3. The cron job produces empty output (Bug 1 masks Bug 2)
4. If Bug 1 is fixed, Bug 2 surfaces as `UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode`

## Related

- Both bugs are in `cron/scheduler.py` `_run_job_script()` function
- Affects all Windows locales with non-UTF-8 system code pages (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, etc.)
- v0.15.2 source confirmed to still have both bugs

# fix(gateway): own-policy adapters fail open without allowlists

## Severity Assessment
### CVSS Assessment

| Metric | v3.1 | v4.0 |
|--------|------|------|
| **Score** | 9.1 / 10.0 | 9.3 / 10.0 |
| **Severity** | Critical | Critical |
| **Vector** | CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N | CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N |
| **Calculator** | [CVSS v3.1 Calculator](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N) | [CVSS v4.0 Calculator](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/4.0#CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) |

### Threat Model Alignment
This crosses the Hermes `SECURITY.md` section 2.6 external-surface allowlist boundary and maps to the section 3.1 `Unauthorized external-surface access` bucket. Gateway adapters that expose network callers must refuse work until an allowlist exists, but own-policy adapters can convert an open intake policy into gateway authorization.

## Impact
With no environment allowlist configured, an own-policy adapter such as QQBot can accept a remote caller under its default-open DM or group policy and the gateway then returns authorized before checking `GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`.

The protected resource is Hermes work dispatch and output delivery across a network-facing gateway adapter.

## Affected Component
**File:** `gateway/run.py:7087-7098`

```python
        if not platform_allowlist and not group_user_allowlist and not group_chat_allowlist and not global_allowlist:
            if self._adapter_enforces_own_access_policy(source.platform):
                return True
            return os.getenv("GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS", "").lower() in {"true", "1", "yes"}
```

Secondary paths:

gateway/platforms/base.py:1850-1869
gateway/platforms/qqbot/adapter.py:210-217
gateway/platforms/qqbot/adapter.py:3139-3151

## Technical Reproduction
1. Against current `main` commit `f66a929a6b78b81bd31a634f05798431b0fb10aa`, enable QQBot with valid credentials and leave all QQ/Gateway allowlists unset.
2. Keep `dm_policy` and `group_policy` omitted so QQBot defaults them to `open`.
3. Send a remote QQ DM or group mention from an unlisted caller.
4. Observe that QQBot intake accepts the event and `GatewayRunner._is_user_authorized()` returns `True` through the own-policy branch.
5. Expected: network adapters deny dispatch until a concrete allowlist exists.

## Demonstrated Impact
- The gateway has a no-allowlist branch that returns `True` for own-policy adapters.
- QQBot's default policy is `open`, not allowlist-only or disabled.
- The adapter allow helpers return `True` for any policy other than `disabled` or `allowlist`.
- This lets an unallowlisted remote caller dispatch Hermes work.

## Environment
Verified against latest upstream `main` via source receipt (`source_ready`, `upstream-main`, `f66a929a6b78b81bd31a634f05798431b0fb10aa`). Full-public submit-fix route is approved for public issue plus linked review-ready PR publication. Redaction checked: no secrets, tokens, credentials, private logs, or unrelated local paths are included.

## Remediation Advice
Keep the gateway default-deny unless the adapter proves a non-empty caller allowlist, or change default own-policy adapter settings from `open` to allowlist-only or disabled.

items.title: [Security] Hermes `skill_view` name traversal discloses files outside the trusted skills directory

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

items.body:
### Advisory Details

**Title**: Hermes `skill_view` name traversal discloses files outside the trusted skills directory

**Description**:

### Summary

Hermes' `skill_view` tool accepts an attacker-controlled `name` and joins it into the trusted skill search roots before enforcing containment. A traversal value such as `../outside-skill` can therefore select a sibling directory that contains `SKILL.md`, after which a benign-looking `file_path` such as `.env` passes the existing linked-file guard and leaks content from outside `~/.hermes/skills/`.

### Details

The vulnerable code path is the real tool dispatch flow reachable through Hermes tool calls. `skill_view` is registered as a normal tool, and attacker-controlled arguments flow through the dispatcher into `tools/skills_tool.py`.

The root cause is in the candidate selection logic. Hermes builds a direct path from the trusted search root and the untrusted `name`, then records that directory as a valid skill if it contains `SKILL.md`:

```python
direct_path = search_dir / name
if direct_path.is_dir() and (direct_path / "SKILL.md").exists():
    _record(direct_path, direct_path / "SKILL.md")
```

Because this happens before any trust-boundary enforcement, `name="../outside-skill"` can resolve to `SKILLS_DIR/../outside-skill` and become the selected `skill_dir`.

Hermes later notices that the chosen skill file is outside the trusted skills directory, but it only logs a warning and does not reject the request. The linked-file path guard is then applied relative to the already escaped `skill_dir`:

```python
target_file = skill_dir / file_path
traversal_error = validate_within_dir(target_file, skill_dir)
```

That means `file_path=".env"` is accepted because it contains no `..`, and `validate_within_dir()` only checks that the target stays inside the attacker-selected escaped directory, not inside the original trusted root.

I verified the issue using the checked-in PoC harness against the real `model_tools.handle_function_call(...)` dispatcher and the real `skill_view` implementation. In the experiment group, Hermes returned:

- `path="../outside-skill/SKILL.md"`
- `content="ESCAPED_SECRET=issue220_variant\n"`

In the control group, changing only the input to `name="legit-skill"` and `file_path="references/api.md"` returned only in-tree content and did not leak the sibling `.env`.

An additional attempt to reproduce through the shipped stdio MCP server is currently blocked by a separate bug in the MCP wrapper schema: `skill_view` is exposed with a required `kwargs` wrapper, but valid requests lose the actual `name` and return `Skill '' not found.`. That wrapper issue does not invalidate this finding because the vulnerable registered tool path is confirmed through Hermes' documented dispatcher.

### PoC

#### Prerequisites

- A checkout of `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- A Python environment that can import Hermes and the `mcp` dependency used by the PoC harness
- Ability to invoke the real Hermes tool dispatcher locally
- No special authentication or non-default Hermes configuration is required

#### Reproduction Steps

1. Download the experiment PoC from: [verification_test.py](https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/5bbf4a2f3fa3b7c3e256f1d4a08f52e1)
2. Download the control PoC from: [control-no-traversal.py](https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/2b024a871d3073ce0e2ebc0f9af683cf)
3. From the repository root, run the experiment PoC:
   `python llm-enhance/cve-finding/InformationLeak/Issue-hermes-agent-220-skill-view-name-traversal-exp/verification_test.py`
4. Observe that the script creates an isolated `HERMES_HOME`, provisions:
   - `skills/legit-skill/SKILL.md`
   - sibling `outside-skill/SKILL.md`
   - sibling `outside-skill/.env`
5. The PoC then invokes the real Hermes dispatcher with:
   - `{"name":"../outside-skill"}`
   - `{"name":"../outside-skill","file_path":".env"}`
6. Run the control PoC:
   `python llm-enhance/cve-finding/InformationLeak/Issue-hermes-agent-220-skill-view-name-traversal-exp/control-no-traversal.py`
7. Confirm the control run only reads `legit-skill/SKILL.md` and `references/api.md`.

### Log of Evidence

Experiment evidence from `observation.log`:

```text
Verification mode: Integration-Test
name-only response: {"success": true, "name": "outside-skill", ... "path": "../outside-skill/SKILL.md", "skill_dir": ".../skills/../outside-skill", ...}
name+.env response: {"success": true, "name": "../outside-skill", "file": ".env", "content": "ESCAPED_SECRET=issue220_variant\n", "file_type": ""}
```

Control evidence from `control-observation.log`:

```text
Control mode: Integration-Test
name-only response: {"success": true, "name": "legit-skill", ... "path": "legit-skill/SKILL.md", ...}
name+reference response: {"success": true, "name": "legit-skill", "file": "references/api.md", "content": "legit reference\n", "file_type": ".md"}
```

MCP wrapper blocker evidence from `mcp-e2e-blocker.log`:

```text
skill_view input schema: {"properties": {"kwargs": {"title": "Kwargs"}}, "required": ["kwargs"], "title": "skill_viewArguments", "type": "object"}
skill_view MCP response: ... "{\"success\": false, \"error\": \"Skill '' not found.\", \"available_skills\": [\"legit-skill\"] ... }"
```

### Impact

This is a path traversal driven information disclosure. Any attacker who can influence `skill_view` arguments through an agent/tool path can make Hermes read files from an attacker-selected sibling or ancestor-controlled directory that contains `SKILL.md`. In practical deployments, that can expose `.env` secrets, model API keys, messaging platform tokens, webhook credentials, private reference files, and other colocated configuration artifacts. The bug crosses the intended trust boundary of `~/.hermes/skills/` and turns a skill viewer into a local secret disclosure primitive.

### Affected products

- **Ecosystem**: pip
- **Package name**: hermes-agent
- **Affected versions**: <= 2026.5.29.2
- **Patched versions**: <None>

### Severity

- **Severity**: High
- **Vector string**: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

### Weaknesses

- **CWE**: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

### Occurrences

| Permalink | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| [https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/77a1650c78a4cb1813d8a81fa1da40a15b6a3ec5/tools/skills_tool.py#L984-L986](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/77a1650c78a4cb1813d8a81fa1da40a15b6a3ec5/tools/skills_tool.py#L984-L986) | `skill_view()` joins attacker-controlled `name` into the trusted search root and records the resulting directory if it contains `SKILL.md`, enabling `../outside-skill` to become a candidate. |
| [https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/77a1650c78a4cb1813d8a81fa1da40a15b6a3ec5/tools/skills_tool.py#L1035-L1036](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/77a1650c78a4cb1813d8a81fa1da40a15b6a3ec5/tools/skills_tool.py#L1035-L1036) | Hermes selects the first recorded candidate as `skill_dir` without rejecting the already escaped directory. |
| [https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/77a1650c78a4cb1813d8a81fa1da40a15b6a3ec5/tools/skills_tool.py#L1062-L1089](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/77a1650c78a4cb1813d8a81fa1da40a15b6a3ec5/tools/skills_tool.py#L1062-L1089) | The code detects that the chosen skill is outside trusted roots, but only emits a warning instead of blocking the request. |
| [https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/77a1650c78a4cb1813d8a81fa1da40a15b6a3ec5/tools/skills_tool.py#L1121-L1140](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/77a1650c78a4cb1813d8a81fa1da40a15b6a3ec5/tools/skills_tool.py#L1121-L1140) | The linked-file guard validates `target_file` relative to the already escaped `skill_dir`, so `.env` passes the check and can be read from outside `SKILLS_DIR`. |
| [https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/77a1650c78a4cb1813d8a81fa1da40a15b6a3ec5/tools/path_security.py#L15-L43](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/77a1650c78a4cb1813d8a81fa1da40a15b6a3ec5/tools/path_security.py#L15-L43) | `validate_within_dir()` and `has_traversal_component()` are generic helpers; they are not sufficient here because the caller supplies a compromised root and a benign `file_path`. |

items.title: Channel Fracture: cron agents silently lose memory write capability (skip_memory=True)

labels.name: area/memory
labels.description: Memory subsystem: store, providers, sync, background reviews

items.body:
## Channel Fracture: Cron agents silently lose memory write capability

### Summary

When a cron job agent attempts to write to persistent memory (via `memory()` or `fact_store()` tools), it fails silently. The cron job completes without error, the agent reports task success, but the memory remains empty. This is caused by two architectural constraints in the cron execution path.

### Root Cause

**Primary (scheduler.py:1652):** The `AIAgent` constructor in cron mode is called with `skip_memory=True`. This flag prevents `_MemoryManager` initialization:

```python
# cron/scheduler.py ~line 1652
AIAgent(
    ...
    skip_memory=True,
    platform="cron",
    ...
)
```

**Secondary (agent/agent_init.py:1168):** Memory tools are registered conditionally — only when `_memory_manager is not None`. Since cron bypasses memory init, the entire memory tool surface is absent:

```python
if agent._memory_manager and agent.tools is not None and (...):
    # memory tool registration — never reached in cron
```

### Impact

- Cron jobs designed to inject knowledge into agent memory **fail silently**
- Writer-side verification passes (cron job created, scheduled, executed)
- Only receiver-side inspection reveals the failure
- No error is propagated to the operator

### Reproduction

1. Create a cron job in any profile that calls `memory(action='add', ...)`
2. Observe: the cron output shows `memory action='add': UNAVAILABLE`
3. Check the target memory store: remains empty
4. The cron exit code is 0 — no error reported

### Suggested Fix

Introduce a **differentiated memory access policy** that separates automatic memory contamination (system prompts) from deliberate tool-call writes:

```python
AIAgent(
    ...
    skip_memory=True,                # Keep blocking auto-contamination
    allow_explicit_memory_writes=True,  # Allow deliberate tool calls
    platform="cron",
    ...
)
```

Alternatively, add a `cron_memory_access` config option per profile that operators can opt into.

### Disclosure

This issue was discovered during production deployment research and is documented in arXiv:2606.04896 (v2 forthcoming with expanded experimental data).

items.title: [Bug]: parse_available_output_tokens_from_error() misses OpenRouter/Nous "in the output" format — causes infinite auto-reset loop

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description

When using OpenRouter-compatible providers (Nous Research inference, OpenRouter itself), the `parse_available_output_tokens_from_error()` function in `agent/model_metadata.py` fails to detect **"output cap too large" errors**, causing a dead loop:

1. User configures `max_tokens` larger than `context_length - input_tokens`
2. Provider returns a 400 error with the **output cap** clearly stated
3. Hermes classifies it as `context_overflow` (correct)
4. But `parse_available_output_tokens_from_error()` returns `None` — it only recognizes Anthropic's `"available_tokens"` keyword, not OpenRouter's `"X in the output"` format
5. Hermes falls through to the **input-too-large recovery path** (compression)
6. On a fresh session with 1 message, compression cannot reduce anything
7. Returns "Context length exceeded (4,882 tokens). Cannot compress further."
8. Gateway auto-resets the session
9. Next message → same error → infinite loop

The user sees "Session auto-reset" repeatedly, and `/new` has no effect because the root cause is the `max_tokens` config value, not the session history.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes to use an OpenRouter/Nous provider with a model that has a 256K context window (e.g., `stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free`)
2. Set `max_tokens: 262000` in config.yaml (exceeding `context_length - input_tokens`)
3. Send ANY message — even "hi" in a brand-new session
4. Observe: API returns 400, Hermes attempts compression, fails, auto-resets the session, loops forever

### Actual API Error (from Nous Research)

```
Error code: 400 - {
  "status": 400,
  "message": "This request is not valid. Check the model name and other parameters. 
    Additional info: This endpoint's maximum context length is 256000 tokens. 
    However, you requested about 281093 tokens 
    (5683 of text input, 13410 of tool input, 262000 in the output). 
    Please reduce the length of either one, or use the context-compression plugin 
    to compress your prompt automatically."
}
```

Breakdown:
| Component | Tokens |
|-----------|--------|
| Text input (system prompt + user msg) | 5,683 |
| Tool schemas | 13,410 |
| **max_tokens (output)** | **262,000** |
| Total requested | 281,093 |
| Model context window | 256,000 |
| **Exceeds by** | **25,093** |

Note: The input (`5683 + 13410 = 19093`) is NOT the problem. The output cap (`262000`) is.

## Expected Behavior

Hermes should:
1. Parse the OpenRouter/Nous error format: extract `maximum context length (256000)`, `text input (5683)`, `tool input (13410)`, and `output (262000)`
2. Detect this is an **output-cap error** (`max_tokens` is the issue, not input)
3. Calculate `available_output = context_length - text_input - tool_input`
4. Auto-reduce `max_tokens` to `available_output - safety_margin` and retry
5. Warn the user: "Output cap (262000) too large for remaining context. Auto-reduced to ~236907."

## Affected Component

- [x] Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)  
- [x] Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp) — the auto-reset loop occurs here

## Root Cause Analysis

### Primary: Missing error format in `parse_available_output_tokens_from_error()`

**File:** `agent/model_metadata.py`, line ~958

The current `is_output_cap_error` guard:

```python
is_output_cap_error = (
    "max_tokens" in error_lower
    and ("available_tokens" in error_lower or "available tokens" in error_lower)
)
```

This only matches Anthropic-style errors (`"... = available_tokens: 10000"`). OpenRouter/Nous use the format:

```
(N of text input, M of tool input, K in the output)
```

This format appears in errors from at least:
- **Nous Research** inference API (`inference-api.nousresearch.com`)
- **OpenRouter** (`openrouter.ai`) — same proxy software

### Secondary: Bad UX — error message is misleading

The final error message seen by the user is:

```
Context length exceeded (4,882 tokens). Cannot compress further.
💡 The conversation has accumulated too much content. 
Try /new to start fresh, or /compress to manually trigger compression.
```

This message implies the **conversation history** is too long (4,882 tokens is tiny). The real fix is to reduce `max_tokens` — but the user has no way to know this. `/new` doesn't reset `max_tokens`, so the loop continues.

### Relevant Architecture Issue

Issue #9181 ("Architecture: separate base vs effective context in overflow recovery") tracks the broader design problem of conflation between input overflow and output-cap overflow. This bug is a concrete, reproducible instance of that conflation causing an infinite loop.

## Proposed Fix

Add OpenRouter/Nous error format support to `parse_available_output_tokens_from_error()`:

```python
# In the is_output_cap_error check:
is_output_cap_error = (
    "max_tokens" in error_lower
    and (
        "available_tokens" in error_lower 
        or "available tokens" in error_lower
        or re.search(r'\d+\s+in\s+the\s+output', error_lower) is not None
    )
)
```

And extract the available output tokens from the OpenRouter format:

```python
# New extraction for OpenRouter/Nous format:
# "5683 of text input, 13410 of tool input, 262000 in the output"
# + "maximum context length is 256000"
or_match = re.search(
    r'maximum\s+context\s+length\s+is\s+(\d+).*?'
    r'(\d+)\s+of\s+text\s+input.*?'
    r'(\d+)\s+of\s+tool\s+input',
    error_lower
)
if or_match:
    max_ctx = int(or_match.group(1))
    text_input = int(or_match.group(2))
    tool_input = int(or_match.group(3))
    available = max_ctx - text_input - tool_input
    if available >= 1:
        return available
```

## Additional Notes

The server-side fix in config is: set `max_tokens` to ≤ `context_length - ~20K` (system prompt + tools overhead), or remove it entirely to let the provider default apply.

## Environment

- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04 (server), Telegram gateway
- **Hermes version:** 0.15.x (installed from source at `/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent`)
- **Model:** `stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free` via Nous Research
- **Provider:** `nous` (OpenRouter-compatible protocol)

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] Yes, I can submit a PR with the regex fix above

labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

The `/claude` command in the gateway fails because it tries to spawn `claude --acp --stdio`, but Claude Code CLI does not support the `--acp` or `--stdio` flags.

The ACP subprocess transport (`agent/copilot_acp_client.py`) was specifically designed for GitHub Copilot CLI (`copilot --acp --stdio`), not Claude Code CLI. This was previously acknowledged in commit 69692039e:

> "The ACP subprocess transport (agent/copilot_acp_client.py) is specifically built for GitHub Copilot CLI ('copilot --acp --stdio')."

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send `/claude` in any gateway chat (Weixin, Telegram, etc.)
2. Send any message (e.g., "who are you")
3. Observe 3 retry attempts, then fallback to fallback model, then 401 error

## Error Log

```
agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 3/3) error_type=RuntimeError
  provider=copilot-acp model=mimo-v2.5-pro
  summary=Copilot ACP process exited early: error: unknown option '--acp'
```

## Root Cause

`gateway/run.py` line 14786-14789:
```python
if self._session_claude_mode.get(session_key):
    runtime_kwargs["provider"] = "copilot-acp"
    runtime_kwargs["command"] = "claude"
    runtime_kwargs["args"] = ["--acp", "--stdio"]
```

Claude Code CLI (`claude --help`) has no `--acp` or `--stdio` flags. The ACP protocol requires a compatible CLI (currently only GitHub Copilot CLI).

## Proposed Fix

Create a lightweight ACP bridge script that:
1. Implements the ACP JSON-RPC protocol on stdin/stdout
2. Translates `session/prompt` requests into `claude -p "prompt"` subprocess calls
3. Returns Claude Code CLI responses as ACP `session/update` chunks

This way the existing `CopilotACPClient` can communicate with Claude Code CLI through the bridge without modifying the ACP client itself.

## Environment

- Claude Code CLI: v2.1.161 (npm install, does NOT have `--acp`)
- Hermes Agent: latest main branch
- Platform: WSL (gateway running via systemd)

items.title: Desktop Remote Gateway should support a true remote workspace/file browser

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes Desktop can connect to a remote backend for chat/session execution, but the Desktop workspace/file browser does not actually operate against that remote backend's filesystem.

In practice, the current Desktop build appears to mix:

- remote session execution/cwd on the backend machine, and
- local Electron file browsing on the Desktop client machine

This makes "workspace" in remote mode feel broken or misleading rather than truly remote-aware.

## Problem

When Hermes Desktop is configured to use a Remote Gateway / remote backend:

- chat/session execution works against the remote machine
- session metadata can carry a remote cwd such as `/Users/...` or `/home/...`
- but the Desktop file browser/workspace pane is backed by local Electron filesystem reads

That means the file browser cannot reliably browse the remote session workspace unless the same remote filesystem is separately mounted onto the local client machine.

Even with a local SSHFS/network-drive mount, the Desktop still has a split-brain model:

- the file browser points at a locally mounted path
- the agent/session cwd still resolves on the remote backend
- attachment/context paths can become local-client paths rather than remote-backend paths

So a mount can be a partial viewing workaround, but it does not provide a coherent remote workspace model.

## Why this matters

Remote mode currently gives the impression that Hermes Desktop is "attached" to the remote machine, but workspace/file browsing is not truly scoped to that same backend.

This causes several UX and correctness problems:

- remote workspace pane may appear empty or unusable for remote POSIX paths
- local and remote path semantics get mixed
- file explorer, terminal, and chat can appear to target the same machine while actually targeting different machines
- local mounts (SSHFS, SMB, etc.) are only a workaround and can drift from the remote agent's actual execution cwd

For remote-development workflows, users need the workspace surface to either:

1. truly browse the selected remote backend filesystem, or
2. be explicitly marked/disabled as local-only in remote mode

## Reproduction

1. Configure Hermes Desktop to use a remote backend on another machine.
2. Confirm chat/session execution is working remotely.
3. Resume or create a session whose cwd resolves to a remote path such as `/Users/...` or `/home/...`.
4. Open the Desktop workspace/file browser.

## Actual behavior

- Remote sessions work.
- Session metadata can contain a remote cwd.
- The Desktop workspace/file browser is still driven by local Electron filesystem reads on the client machine.
- Remote paths are not first-class in the file browser/workspace experience.

## Expected behavior

One of these should happen:

1. **Remote-native workspace support**
   - File browser/workspace pane reads directories through the selected remote backend/gateway.
   - Attachments/context refs created from the workspace are usable by the remote agent without path mismatch.
   - Terminal/file browser/chat all share the same backend target.

2. **Explicit local-only fallback**
   - In remote mode, the file browser/workspace pane is clearly labeled as local-only and does not pretend to represent the remote backend workspace.
   - Ideally disabled by default unless the user intentionally opts into a local-mounted path workflow.

## Evidence from current implementation

From local inspection of the packaged Desktop app:

- the file browser uses the Electron preload `readDir` bridge
- the Electron main process handles directory reads via local `fs.promises.readdir(...)`
- session creation/cwd updates are sent to the remote backend separately

So the Desktop currently combines:

- local client filesystem browsing, and
- remote backend session cwd/execution

rather than a single remote workspace contract.

## Related issues

- #38369 Desktop Remote Gateway should make Terminal/File Explorer execution target explicit
- #38464 Desktop drag-drop file uploads don't sync to remote gateway workspace
- #37876 feat(desktop): support local and remote Hermes backends simultaneously

This issue is narrower than #37876 and more concrete than #38369: it requests first-class remote workspace/file browser behavior (or an explicit local-only fallback) for Desktop remote mode.

items.title: Desktop: add project_id-based session grouping (WebUI parity)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes Desktop would benefit from WebUI-style session grouping by project, ideally using a session-level `project_id` so operators can organize many concurrent sessions across long-lived projects.

I realize Hermes already uses `project_id` in some integration contexts (for example Bitwarden / GCP-related settings), so if that name is too overloaded I would still strongly support a session-specific variant. But from an operator UX perspective, the core request is:

- assign a session to a project
- filter the Desktop sidebar by project
- create / rename / delete projects from the UI
- preserve project assignment across session continuation / compression

## Why this matters

Hermes Desktop is becoming the main operator surface for remote / always-on Hermes setups.

In that workflow, we often have:

- one long-running Hermes backend on a remote host
- many concurrent sessions
- multiple real projects sharing the same Desktop surface
- kanban / handoff / status workflows outside the immediate chat transcript

Right now, Desktop already has:

- sessions
- titles
- search
- pinning
- grouping by workspace / cwd

But it does not yet have a first-class "this session belongs to project X" concept in the UI.

Using cwd or title conventions as a substitute is not enough for operators managing:

- multiple repos under one broader project
- many sessions within one repo
- long-lived project tracking over time
- project-specific filters for triage / handoff / resume

## Request

Please add WebUI-style project grouping for Desktop sessions.

### Ideal UX

- A `Projects` row or chip bar in the Desktop sidebar
- `All` plus user-defined projects
- Create project inline
- Rename / delete project
- Assign / unassign session to project from the session row menu
- Filter sessions by selected project
- Optional project color

### Desired behavior

- Project assignment survives compression / continuation chains
- Works with remote backends, not only local Desktop installs
- Shows up in search results and session metadata where appropriate
- Can be used alongside existing workspace grouping, not necessarily replacing it

## Suggested implementation direction

I think this is most useful as a backend-backed session metadata feature, not only a Desktop-local preference layer.

Reasons:

- session grouping should survive across Desktop restarts
- it should work with remote backends
- it should be available to future CLI / kanban / command-center workflows
- it should not depend only on the local Desktop machine

So my preference would be:

- add a nullable project field to session metadata
- expose it in session list / search / patch APIs
- add a small project registry for names/colors
- wire it into the Desktop sidebar

## Naming

My first request would be to support `project_id` because that is already an intuitive and proven model from Hermes WebUI-style session organization.

That said, if maintainers feel bare `project_id` is too overloaded because Hermes already uses that term in other integration contexts, I would still consider these acceptable:

- `session_project_id`
- `project_group_id`
- `workspace_project_id`

The important part is the feature, not the exact field name.

## Why this is especially useful for kanban / operator workflows

For operator-style use, a project grouping layer helps align:

- session list
- project status / handoff
- kanban board ownership
- multi-project remote Desktop operations

Without this, Desktop is great for chatting and searching, but still weak as a project-oriented control surface when many sessions accumulate.

## Concrete ask

If full backend support is too large for one step, even a staged rollout would be valuable:

1. Desktop-only project grouping MVP
2. backend-backed session metadata
3. API support
4. command center / kanban integration

I would be happy with either:

- a direct Desktop feature
- or a broader "session project grouping" feature that Desktop exposes first

Thanks — this would make Hermes Desktop much more viable as the main surface for serious multi-project operator workflows.

items.title: `_is_local_backend()` doesn't consider terminal.backend — intentional?
items.body:
## Description

When `terminal.backend` is set to docker, the terminal runs in a container with network isolation. But `_is_local_backend()` only checks `browser.cloud_provider`, so the SSRF guard still gets skipped — browser on host can freely access internal networks that the terminal can't.

```python
def _is_local_backend() -> bool:
    return _is_camofox_mode() or _get_cloud_provider() is None
```

So "local backend" here actually means "local browser", not "local terminal". In docker/daytona/modal scenarios, the two don't match — terminal is sandboxed but browser isn't.

The practical concern: services listening on `127.0.0.1` on the host (databases, dev servers, internal APIs) are exposed to the agent via browser navigation, even though the user explicitly chose a containerized terminal presumably to prevent this kind of access.

This feels like unexpected behavior. Is it a known trade-off, or should `terminal.backend` be factored into the guard? I didn't find existing discussion about this specific gap (#16234 covers cloud metadata, #4281 is the opposite direction). If it's intentional, a note in the docs would help users understand that container isolation doesn't extend to browser navigation.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Set `terminal.backend: docker` in config
2. On the host, start any service on `127.0.0.1` (e.g. `python -m http.server 8080 --bind 127.0.0.1`)
3. Ask the agent to `browser_navigate("http://127.0.0.1:8080")`

## Expected Behavior
Navigation should be blocked (or at least warned), since the user chose a containerized terminal to isolate the agent from the host network.

## Actual Behavior
Navigation succeeds. `_is_local_backend()` returns `True` (because `cloud_provider` is None), SSRF guard is skipped entirely, and the agent can freely reach host-local services that the docker terminal itself cannot access.

items.title: Nous auth JWT overrides custom provider API key, causing 403 on third-party endpoints
items.body:
## Bug Description

When using a custom provider (e.g. `custom_providers` in config.yaml pointing to a third-party OpenAI-compatible endpoint), the Nous inference auth system injects a JWT token as the API key, overriding the user-configured key. This causes 403 "Your request was blocked" errors on endpoints that dont accept Nous JWT tokens.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a custom provider in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   custom_providers:
   - api_key: sk-xxxxx
     base_url: https://some-third-party.com/v1
     model: gpt-4o
     name: "MyProvider"
   ```
2. Make sure Nous auth is active (logged in via `hermes setup`)
3. Switch to the custom provider and send a message
4. Request fails with HTTP 403

## Expected Behavior

Custom providers should use the user-configured API key from `custom_providers[].api_key`, NOT the Nous JWT token. The Nous auth system should only apply to Nous-native providers (e.g. `provider: nous` or Nous inference endpoints).

## Actual Behavior

Logs show:
```
Nous inference auth: using NAS invoke JWT
OpenAI client created ... provider=custom base_url=https://some-third-party.com/v1
Streaming failed before delivery: Your request was blocked.
```

The Nous JWT is being sent as the `Authorization: Bearer` header to the third-party endpoint, which correctly rejects it with 403.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent version: latest (installed via git)
- OS: macOS 26.5
- Python: 3.11
- OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0

## Logs

```
WARNING run_agent: Credential pool provider mismatch: pool=custom:君の公益, agent=custom — skipping pool mutation to avoid cross-provider contamination
WARNING agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=PermissionDeniedError provider=custom base_url=https://muyuan.do/v1 model=gpt-5.5 summary=HTTP 403: Your request was blocked.
ERROR agent.conversation_loop: Non-retryable client error: Your request was blocked.
```

## Suggested Fix

In the auth resolution path, skip Nous JWT injection when the resolved provider is `custom` and the base_url does not match a known Nous inference endpoint.

items.title: [Feature] Extend goal_mode judge gate to kanban_block (symmetric with kanban_complete)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
# Draft Issue — extend goal-mode judge gate to `kanban_block`

## Title
`[Feature] Extend goal_mode judge gate to kanban_block (symmetric with kanban_complete)`

## Body

### Context

PR #38388 (fixes #38367) adds a judge gate to `_handle_complete` so a worker cannot prematurely close a `goal_mode` task via `kanban_complete` without the auxiliary judge confirming the terminal verdict.

`kanban_block(reason="...")` is a symmetric exit path from the goal loop: it transitions the task to `blocked` and the goal-loop logic treats that as terminal in the same way it treats `done`. A worker that has learned the complete path is gated will naturally route through block instead, achieving the same premature exit.

### Repro

1. Create a kanban task with `goal_mode=True` and a body specifying terminal criteria.
2. Dispatch a worker.
3. Worker calls `kanban_block(reason="anything")` mid-loop.
4. Task status → `blocked`, goal loop exits without judge verdict on the actual goal criteria.

### Proposal

Two options, in order of preference:

**Option A — judge gate on block when goal_mode=True**

Mirror the PR #38388 pattern in `_handle_block`:

```python
if task.goal_mode:
    try:
        verdict = judge_goal(
            title=task.title,
            body=task.body,
            outcome_kind="blocked",
            reason=reason,
        )
        if verdict not in ("blocked_human_input", "blocked_dependency"):
            return error("Goal block rejected by judge: ...")
    except Exception:
        # fail-open with metric, matching PR #38388 behavior
        ...
```

The judge accepts only verdicts that map to legitimate non-completion terminals (`blocked_human_input`, `blocked_dependency`). Anything else routes back through the complete path → which is now gated.

**Option B — block reason allowlist under goal_mode**

Simpler, no extra LLM call:

```python
GOAL_MODE_BLOCK_ALLOWLIST = {"blocked_human_input", "blocked_dependency"}

if task.goal_mode and reason not in GOAL_MODE_BLOCK_ALLOWLIST:
    return error(f"In goal_mode, block reason must be one of {GOAL_MODE_BLOCK_ALLOWLIST}")
```

Cheaper, deterministic, but workers can still pass an allowed reason without it being truthful. Pairs well with a downstream review step.

### Why this matters

Goal mode is the autonomous-execution primitive in kanban. Any unguarded exit path is functionally a complete bypass — it does not matter to the dispatcher whether the goal exited as `done` or `blocked`, the loop is gone either way. PR #38388 only closes one of the two.

### Related

- PR #38388 (kanban_complete judge gate) — sibling fix
- Issue #38367 (kanban_complete bypass) — original report
- Issue #38366 (max_runtime_seconds=0 silent kill) — separate goal-mode adjacent bug

### Acceptance criteria

- A `goal_mode=True` task whose worker calls `kanban_block` with an off-allowlist reason should remain `running` (or whatever state pre-gate).
- A test analogous to `test_complete_goal_mode_rejected_by_judge` for the block path.
- Documentation in the goal-mode user guide noting that `goal_mode` constrains both complete and block paths.

items.title: "session not found" when Gateway restarts during active Desktop session

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug: "session not found" when Gateway restarts during active Desktop session

### Environment
- **OS:** macOS 26.5.1
- **Hermes version:** Latest (installed via bootstrap)
- **Desktop app:** Hermes.app (Electron)
- **Provider:** DeepSeek (deepseek-v4-pro)

### Summary
When the Hermes Gateway backend process restarts (auto-restart, crash, or update cycle) while a Desktop/TUI session is active, the session state is lost from memory. The Desktop app sends the old session ID to the new Gateway process, which returns "session not found". The error then **persists/sticks** at the bottom of the UI and does not auto-clear — it remains visible even after switching to a new conversation.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Start Hermes Desktop and begin a conversation (session A)
2. Wait for or trigger a Gateway restart (`SIGTERM` → new PID)
3. Continue typing in session A within the Desktop app
4. Observe "session not found" error

### Reproduced Timeline (from logs)
```
2026-06-04 03:38 UTC  →  Session 20260604_113841_971ded created (user chatting)
2026-06-04 03:52 UTC  →  Gateway PID 3237 exits with `exit_nonzero` (gateway-exit-diag.log)
2026-06-04 03:52 UTC  →  Gateway restarts as PID 28990
                       →  Desktop app sends old session_id to new Gateway → "session not found"
```

### Root Cause Analysis
1. **Session state is in-memory only.** Active sessions are held in the Gateway process memory. When Gateway restarts (which happens roughly every ~24h based on `gateway-exit-diag.log`), all active sessions are lost. The SQLite session store (`~/.hermes/state.db`) persists completed sessions but the live session state is not checkpointed to survive a restart.

2. **Desktop app does not handle the error gracefully.** When the backend returns "session not found", the error message gets stuck in the UI and does not auto-dismiss. There's no automatic recovery (e.g., "Your session was lost, starting a new one").

### Expected Behavior
- **Option A:** Session state should survive Gateway restarts (persist active sessions to disk, or use the SQLite store as the source of truth even for live sessions).
- **Option B:** If session recovery is not feasible, the Desktop/TUI client should detect "session not found" and gracefully offer to start a new session, clearing the error.

### Log Evidence
**desktop.log** — shows SIGTERM + restart cycle:
```
Hermes backend exited (SIGTERM)
[boot] Resolving Hermes backend
[boot] Starting Hermes backend ...
[boot] Hermes backend is ready
```

**gateway-exit-diag.log** — daily exit_nonzero pattern:
```json
{"ts": "2026-06-04T03:52:21.440685+00:00", "tag": "gateway.exit_nonzero", "pid": 3237}
{"ts": "2026-06-04T03:52:23.868340+00:00", "tag": "gateway.start", "pid": 28990}
```

**agent.log** — the user's message hitting the dead session:
```
agent.conversation_loop: conversation turn: session=20260604_115530_dab9fa
  model=deepseek-v4-pro provider=deepseek platform=tui history=42 msg='session not found'
```

### Additional Context
- The Gateway restart pattern (`exit_nonzero` approximately every 24h) appears to be a scheduled recycle rather than a crash — `sys_exc` is `(None, None, None)` at exit time, suggesting intentional shutdown (possibly memory-pressure triggered or auto-update related).
- This affects both Desktop and TUI users, as both connect to the same Gateway backend.
